claims.text: Interface coherency significantly influences the transition between diffusion-mediated and dislocation-mediated creep in high-entropy alloy multilayers.
Increasing interface coherency enhances resistance to dislocation motion in high-entropy alloy multilayers.
Controlled deposition techniques can manipulate interface coherency in high-entropy alloy multilayers.
Creep behavior is prominent under the proposed high-temperature conditions.
Increasing interface coherency restricts dislocation movement.
Restriction of dislocation movement favors diffusion-mediated creep over dislocation-mediated creep.
High-entropy alloy multilayers with higher interface coherency will exhibit lower creep rates than multilayers with low interface coherency.
The proposed relationship applies specifically to high-entropy alloy multilayers under high-temperature conditions.
The effects of interface coherency on creep may vary among alloy compositions.
